lines.text: Here's how to build an agent that briefs you every morning, in under sixty seconds.
A daily brief agent reads your Slack and GitHub on a schedule, and posts one short summary.
Say it's Tuesday: a hundred and forty messages, twenty-five pull requests.
Step one: agent dot M D. A model, its tools, and the steps, in plain English.
The key rule: only put something in the brief if you need to act on it today.
Step two: deployment dot M D. Weekdays at seven thirty-two, with a five dollar cap per run.
Step three: memory: two folders kept between runs. Your preferences, which it can read but never change. And its own notes, like a bookmark for each source.
A bookmark marks where it stopped reading. So even if a run is late, it starts right there, and nothing slips through.
Then run ant apply, and every weekday morning, the brief arrives.
If a source can't be read, the brief says so, instead of looking like a quiet day.
